financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone parent-entity, holding company) basis. revenue = 'Revenue from contracts with customers' (1,786,450) + 'Other revenue' (1,153) = 1,787,603, equal to the printed Gross profit line since Company-level cost of sales is nil (a holding company with no direct cost of sales). No income tax expense at Company level this period (nil, as printed) -- PBT = PAT (1,283,512), a large jump from Rs.140,947k a year earlier, driven almost entirely by higher 'Revenue from contracts with customers' (1,786,450 vs 498,079, +259% YoY) which most likely reflects dividend/management-fee-type income from subsidiaries rather than third-party trading (this is a holding company, not an operating entity). EPS 0.63 = 1,283,512 / 2,035,038,000, matches printed. short_term_borrowings = 'Short term borrowings' (15,959,500) -- no separate current interest-bearing loans line at Company level. long_term_borrowings = 0 (no non-current interest-bearing borrowings at Company level; the entire non-current liabilities balance of 86,516 is employee benefit liabilities). capex left unset (None) for the same reason as the Group row -- the condensed cash flow statement gives only a single combined investing-activities line with no PPE/capex breakdown.

Group basis. revenue = 'Total Revenue' (19,965,911) = revenue from contracts with customers (18,669,113) + revenue from insurance contracts (319,586) + interest revenue (977,212) -- all three lines are printed above a 'Total Revenue' subtotal (pg.5), used as-is rather than just the contracts-with-customers line, consistent with this being a diversified group with a financial-services/insurance segment. profit_before_tax/tax_expense/profit_after_tax: the income statement's continuing-operations PBT (1,568,171) and tax (782,561) chain to a continuing PAT of 785,610, but the printed 'Profit for the period' total is 785,228 (a Rs.382k discontinued-operations after-tax loss lower) -- profit_after_tax uses the total 785,228 figure (the filing's own headline number) while profit_before_tax and tax_expense use the continuing-only figures as printed (no separate PBT/tax split is given for the discontinued piece, which is disclosed net-of-tax only). The resulting ~0.02% PBT-minus-tax vs PAT gap is the discontinued operations loss, not an extraction error. EPS 0.27 = 553,820 (profit attributable to equity holders of the parent) / 2,035,038,000 shares (note 4.1, pg.11: 2,035,038 thousand ordinary shares) -- matches printed EPS exactly. short_term_borrowings = Interest-bearing loans and borrowings, current (5,147,351) + Short term borrowings (28,187,196) = 33,334,547; Public Deposits (12,114,227, a finance-company deposit-taking liability tied to the Group's Financial Services segment) are EXCLUDED from short_term_borrowings since they are a separately labelled liability line, not conventional bank/market debt -- flagged as a judgment call. long_term_borrowings = Interest-bearing loans and borrowings, non-current, only (3,806,320) -- lease liabilities (current 1,853,308 + non-current 2,809,420) excluded as a separate line. capex is left unset (None): the cash flow statement (pg.9) is heavily condensed and gives only a single summary line 'Net cash flows used in investing activities' (-62,024) with no breakdown into PPE acquisition, disposals, or other components -- a genuine disclosure gap, see gaps_note in interim_updates.

thesis.thesis_text: Richard Pieris and Company PLC (RICH) is a large, diversified Sri Lankan conglomerate spanning Rubber, Plastic/Furniture/Electronics, Retail, Tyre, and Financial Services. Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026) revenue grew 5.9% YoY to Rs.19,965.9mn with broadly flat operating profit (-2.1% to Rs.1,836.8mn), but profit attributable to equity holders fell 43.8% to Rs.553.8mn because finance costs surged 77.1% YoY to Rs.695.9mn and tax expense rose 44.8% to Rs.782.6mn -- a below-the-line story rather than an operating deterioration. Segment performance was genuinely mixed: Rubber turned around from an operating loss to a Rs.255.6mn profit on 21.8% revenue growth, while Tyre weakened sharply (revenue -29.3%, profit -44.2%) and Retail, the largest segment, saw profit fall 29.2% despite revenue growth, a margin story the filing does not explain. At Rs.27.00, the stock trades at an approximate 25.0x run-rate P/E -- rich against this quarter's profit decline -- though a roughly 4.8% dividend yield (FY2025 DPS Rs.1.30) provides some support, tempered by an uneven three-year dividend history. An unexplained Rs.1,129.3mn operating profit in the 'Other services' segment against just Rs.11.7mn of external revenue, largely offset by a Rs.1,492.1mn inter-segment elimination, is a segmental transparency concern worth following up (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id manual_484cc416a73c2672, p.5 and p.11).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no rubber/tyre commodity-price or Sri Lanka consumer-retail sector data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence benefits from a three-year dividend history (FY2023-FY2025) but is otherwise limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period P&L trend), the cash flow statement is too condensed to populate capex, and the 'Other services' segment's disproportionate operating profit relative to its external revenue is not explained by the filing.

financial_quality.rationale: Richard Pieris and Company PLC (RICH) is a large diversified group (total assets Rs.113,587.5mn, equity Rs.35,687.9mn) with total liabilities of Rs.77,899.6mn (Debt/Equity ~2.18x), including Rs.33,334.5mn of interest-bearing short-term borrowings and Rs.12,114.2mn of finance-company public deposits tied to its Financial Services segment. Current ratio is thin at 1.12x (current assets Rs.68,507.0mn / current liabilities Rs.61,178.7mn). Quarterly ROE attributable to equity holders is modest at approximately 1.55% (annualised ~6.2%). Group operating profit was broadly flat YoY (-2.1% to Rs.1,836.8mn) but profit attributable to equity holders fell 43.8% to Rs.553.8mn because finance costs surged 77.1% YoY to Rs.695.9mn and tax expense rose 44.8% to Rs.782.6mn -- leverage-cost and tax burden, not operating performance, drove the bottom-line decline.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group revenue grew a genuine 5.9% YoY to Rs.19,965.9mn, with a clear operational turnaround in Rubber (operating loss of Rs.34.5mn swinging to a Rs.255.6mn profit on 21.8% revenue growth) and growth in Plastic/Furniture/Electronics (+31.1% revenue, +21.2% profit). This was offset by a sharp Tyre segment weakening (revenue -29.3%, profit -44.2%) and a margin-compression story in the largest segment, Retail (revenue +4.6% but profit -29.2%, cause not detailed in the filing). Net, operating profit was roughly flat (-2.1%) despite the revenue growth, and the entire bottom-line decline (attributable PAT -43.8%) came from below the operating line (finance costs, tax).

valuation.rationale: At Rs.27.00 (2026-08-31, market cap Rs.53,928.5mn), annualising this quarter's attributable EPS (Rs.0.27 x4 = Rs.1.08) implies a P/E of approximately 25.0x, rich for a quarter where attributable profit fell 43.8% YoY; P/B is approximately 1.51x on equity of Rs.35,687.9mn. Dividend yield based on the FY2025 DPS of Rs.1.30 is approximately 4.8%, though the dividend history (Rs.0.70 FY2023, Rs.0.50 FY2024, Rs.1.30 FY2025) has not been smoothly growing, so the yield should not be read as a stable, compounding income stream.
citations: dividends: FY2025 DPS 1.30, FY2024 DPS 0.50, FY2023 DPS 0.70

business_quality.rationale: RICH is a large, genuinely diversified conglomerate spanning Rubber, Plastic/Furniture/Electronics, Retail (its largest segment by revenue, likely including the Arpico retail chain), Tyre, and Financial Services/insurance -- diversification that provides some resilience, as this quarter's Rubber turnaround demonstrates even while Tyre weakened sharply. However, the segmental note shows an 'Other services' segment with a disproportionate Rs.1,129.3mn operating profit against only Rs.11.7mn of external revenue, largely offset by a Rs.1,492.1mn inter-segment elimination (vs Rs.227.9mn PY) that the filing does not explain -- an opacity flag that limits how cleanly the Group's true segment economics can be assessed.

governance_risk.rationale: RICH has a multi-year dividend track record (FY2023-FY2025 DPS on file), a positive governance signal for a large, long-established listed group. However, the unexplained scale of the 'Other services' segment's operating profit relative to its external revenue, and the large jump in inter-segment eliminations YoY, reduce segmental transparency. No disclosures/circulars feed exists in this project to independently verify board or ownership changes.

key_reasons: Group revenue grew 5.9% YoY to Rs.19,965.9mn and operating profit was broadly flat (-2.1%), but profit attributable to equity holders fell 43.8% to Rs.553.8mn because finance costs surged 77.1% YoY to Rs.695.9mn and tax expense rose 44.8% to Rs.782.6mn -- a below-the-operating-line story, not an operating deterioration

Segment performance is genuinely mixed: Rubber turned around from a loss to a Rs.255.6mn profit on 21.8% revenue growth and Plastic/Furniture/Electronics grew both revenue and profit, but Tyre weakened sharply (revenue -29.3%, profit -44.2%) and Retail (the largest segment) saw profit fall 29.2% despite revenue growth

At ~25.0x run-rate P/E, valuation looks rich against a quarter where attributable profit fell 43.8%, though a ~4.8% dividend yield (FY2025 DPS Rs.1.30) provides some support -- the dividend history is not smoothly growing, so should not be treated as a stable income stream
watch_factors: Finance costs rose 77.1% YoY to Rs.695.9mn -- if this leveraged cost base persists or grows further, it will continue to compress attributable profit even if operating performance stabilises
Retail segment (largest by revenue) saw profit fall 29.2% despite 4.6% revenue growth -- the filing gives no explanation for this margin compression, worth seeking clarification in future disclosures

The 'Other services' segment's Rs.1,129.3mn operating profit against only Rs.11.7mn of external revenue, largely offset by a Rs.1,492.1mn inter-segment elimination, is unexplained by the filing -- a segmental transparency concern to monitor

horizon_notes.6m: Q2 FY2026/27 results will show whether the Rubber turnaround continues, whether Tyre stabilises, and whether finance costs continue to outpace operating profit growth.
horizon_notes.1y: If finance costs moderate (e.g., through deleveraging or rate relief) while the Rubber and Plastic/Furniture/Electronics segments' growth continues, attributable PAT could recover meaningfully from this quarter's depressed base.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether RICH's diversified segment mix (particularly Retail's margin and Tyre's competitive position) can generate durable growth once leverage costs are brought under control -- not yet testable with one quarter of interim data.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/consumer-spending or rubber/tyre commodity-price data source exists in this project to assess RICH's multi-year segment trajectory.

interim_updates.note_text: Richard Pieris and Company PLC (RICH) reported Group revenue of Rs.19,965.9mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), up 5.9% YoY from Rs.18,858.3mn, while Group operating profit was broadly flat at Rs.1,836.8mn (-2.1% YoY from Rs.1,877.0mn) and profit attributable to equity holders of the parent fell sharply, down 43.8% YoY to Rs.553.8mn from Rs.985.6mn. The decline was driven below the operating-profit line: finance costs surged 77.1% YoY to Rs.(695.9)mn from Rs.(393.1)mn, and income tax expense rose 44.8% YoY to Rs.782.6mn from Rs.540.5mn, together pulling PBT down 10.0% to Rs.1,568.2mn and PAT down 34.6% to Rs.785.2mn even though the underlying operating businesses held up close to flat. By segment (pg.11 note), the standout mover was Rubber, which swung from an operating loss of Rs.(34.5)mn to a profit of Rs.255.6mn on 21.8% revenue growth to Rs.1,668.9mn (from Rs.1,370.1mn) -- the clearest genuine operational turnaround in the quarter. Tyre was the weak spot: revenue fell 29.3% YoY to Rs.943.4mn and segment operating profit fell 44.2% to Rs.115.7mn. Plastic, Furniture and Electronics grew revenue 31.1% YoY to Rs.3,526.3mn with profit up 21.2% to Rs.464.2mn. Retail grew revenue 4.6% YoY to Rs.8,887.7mn but segment profit fell 29.2% to Rs.319.8mn -- a clear margin story in the Group's largest segment by revenue. The 'Other services' segment shows an operating profit of Rs.1,129.3mn on just Rs.11.7mn of external revenue (vs a Rs.(65.3)mn loss a year earlier); this is disproportionate to the segment's own trading activity and, per the segmental note's own 'Inter segment eliminations' line, is largely offset at Group level (eliminations of Rs.(1,492.1)mn this quarter vs only Rs.(227.9)mn a year earlier) -- consistent with most of this figure being an intra-group/allocation item rather than a clean external profit contributor, and it is NOT treated as a genuine driver of Group profit growth in this note (see gaps_note).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements entry for RICH in this database, so no prior quarter (e.g. Q4 FY2025/26, quarter ended 31 March 2026) is available for a sequential comparison -- only the filing's own YoY comparative column is used. Genuine disclosure gaps: (1) the cash flow statement (pg.9) is heavily condensed, giving only single summary lines for investing and financing activities with no breakdown of capex/PPE acquisitions, so capex is not populated in financial_statements for either basis; (2) the 'Other services' segment's Rs.1,129.3mn operating profit (vs only Rs.11.7mn external revenue) is not explained by any note in this filing -- the segmental table shows a Rs.(1,492.1)mn Group-level inter-segment elimination this quarter (vs Rs.(227.9)mn a year earlier) that appears to offset most of it, consistent with an intra-group/allocation effect, but the filing does not identify the underlying transaction, so this could not be attributed to a specific driver and was excluded from the key_drivers list; (3) the Retail segment's 29.2% profit decline despite revenue growth is not explained by any commentary in the filing (e.g. no mention of input cost pressure, discounting, or a specific product line) -- flagged as an unexplained margin item rather than assigned a cause.
interim_updates.takeaway: Group profit attributable to equity holders fell 43.8% YoY despite revenue growth (+5.9%) and broadly flat operating profit (-2.1%) because the decline sits below the operating line: finance costs jumped 77.1% YoY to Rs.695.9mn and tax expense rose 44.8% to Rs.782.6mn. Operationally, Rubber genuinely turned around (loss to Rs.255.6mn profit on 21.8% revenue growth), Plastic/Furniture/Electronics grew both revenue and profit, but Tyre weakened sharply (revenue -29.3%, profit -44.2%) and Retail's margin compressed (revenue +4.6% but profit -29.2%) -- a mixed operating picture, with the finance-cost and tax burden the dominant reason the headline profit number looks worse than the underlying businesses.
operational_highlights: Group revenue up 5.9% YoY to Rs.19,965.9mn (from Rs.18,858.3mn); operating profit broadly flat at Rs.1,836.8mn (-2.1% YoY from Rs.1,877.0mn)
Profit attributable to equity holders of the parent fell 43.8% YoY to Rs.553.8mn (from Rs.985.6mn); EPS fell to Rs.0.27 from Rs.0.48

Rubber segment (pg.11 note) swung from an operating loss of Rs.(34.5)mn to a profit of Rs.255.6mn, on revenue growth of 21.8% YoY to Rs.1,668.9mn (from Rs.1,370.1mn) -- the clearest genuine operational turnaround this quarter
Tyre segment weakened sharply: revenue -29.3% YoY to Rs.943.4mn, segment operating profit -44.2% to Rs.115.7mn (from Rs.207.3mn)
Plastic, Furniture and Electronics segment: revenue +31.1% YoY to Rs.3,526.3mn, profit +21.2% to Rs.464.2mn
Retail segment (largest by revenue): revenue +4.6% YoY to Rs.8,887.7mn, but segment profit fell 29.2% to Rs.319.8mn (from Rs.451.6mn) -- a margin compression story despite top-line growth

Finance costs up 77.1% YoY to Rs.(695.9)mn (from Rs.(393.1)mn) and income tax expense up 44.8% YoY to Rs.782.6mn (from Rs.540.5mn) -- together the dominant reason PAT fell 34.6% even as operating profit was roughly flat

'Other services' segment operating profit of Rs.1,129.3mn on only Rs.11.7mn of external revenue is disproportionate and appears largely offset by a Rs.(1,492.1)mn inter-segment elimination at Group level (vs Rs.(227.9)mn a year earlier) -- flagged as likely an intra-group/allocation item, not treated as a genuine external profit driver
key_drivers: Finance costs rose 77.1% YoY to Rs.695.9mn (from Rs.393.1mn) -- the single largest driver of the gap between broadly flat operating profit (-2.1%) and the much sharper 43.8% fall in profit attributable to equity holders
Income tax expense rose 44.8% YoY to Rs.782.6mn (from Rs.540.5mn), compounding the finance-cost drag on PAT

Rubber segment turned around from a Rs.(34.5)mn operating loss to a Rs.255.6mn profit on 21.8% revenue growth (Rs.1,668.9mn from Rs.1,370.1mn) -- the strongest genuine segment-level improvement, per the operating segment note (pg.11)

Retail segment profit fell 29.2% YoY to Rs.319.8mn despite revenue growing 4.6% to Rs.8,887.7mn -- margin compression in the Group's largest segment by revenue, direction/cause not detailed further in this filing
